comparison: Perfect agreement on genomic location claims (C1, C10, C11, C12). Both evaluations find the genomic mapping data well-supported across multiple species.
Perfect agreement on compensatory upregulation claims (C64-C68). Both recognize this as important for understanding why multiple knockouts were needed to observe phenotypes.

Strong agreement on testis-specific expression claims (C33-C37). OpenEval provides detailed support from small RNA-seq data; peer reviewers affirm testis-specific expression as foundational for functional studies.

Strong agreement on knockout phenotype claims (C4, C38-C42). Both find the litter size reduction supported, though OpenEval notes the phenotype is subtle while peer reviewers emphasize evolutionary significance.
Strong agreement on sperm competition claims (C44-C51). Both evaluations find the multiple experimental approaches (sequential mating, IVF, co-AI) convincing and well-supported.
Agreement on IVF mechanistic findings (C52-C54). OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation; peer reviewers accept these as supporting the sperm competition defect mechanism.

Agreement on conservation and divergence claims (C13-C22). OpenEval focuses on PhyloP/PhastCons statistical support for C13-C16; peer reviewers group broader evolutionary findings including C17-C22, affirming rapid evolution.

Overlapping evolutionary claims (C20-C22). OpenEval evaluates 1000 Genomes data separately; peer reviewers integrate this with broader conservation analysis as part of comprehensive evolutionary characterization.
Overlapping evolutionary claims (C17-C19). OpenEval evaluates substitution patterns separately; peer reviewers include these in broader evolutionary narrative supporting rapid evolution.
Agreement on evolutionary timing claims (C23-C24). OpenEval focuses on phylogenetic evidence; peer reviewers integrate this with MER91C origin findings.
Agreement on MER91C origin claims (C25-C27, C32). OpenEval provides detailed validation of BLAST and phylogenetic evidence; peer reviewers explicitly affirm MER91C transposon origin.
Agreement on miRNA biogenesis claims (C28-C31). OpenEval notes heterologous system limitation; peer reviewers affirm that human MER91C produces mature miRNAs in cultured cells.

Agreement on transcriptomic impact claims (C55-C61). OpenEval raises concerns about large number of DETs and whole testis confounding; peer reviewers accept RNA-seq findings and Crisp1 target validation.
Agreement on target validation claims (C59-C61). OpenEval notes complexity of opposite effects from different miRNAs; peer reviewers accept validation approaches supporting Crisp1 as key target.
Agreement on Crisp1 phenocopy claims (C62-C63). OpenEval notes appropriate use of literature; peer reviewers accept this comparison as providing mechanistic context.
Agreement on target conservation claims (C69-C72). OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation; peer reviewers accept comparative target analysis and purifying selection interpretation.
Partial overlap on human-mouse targeting differences (C73-C78, C80). OpenEval evaluates increased targeting per miRNA; peer reviewers group with broader evolutionary divergence in targeting.
Agreement on human targeting expansion claims (C75-C77). OpenEval notes reliance on computational predictions; peer reviewers accept as part of evolutionary analysis.
Agreement on selective pressure claim (C80). OpenEval finds conclusion reasonable but speculative; peer reviewers accept as part of evolutionary narrative.
Agreement on MER91C transcript control analysis (C79). Both find this important for ruling out alternative explanations of increased targeting.
Agreement on ortholog identification claims (C89-C92). OpenEval notes speculative functional interpretation; peer reviewers accept as part of comprehensive evolutionary framework.
Different evaluation on ADAR editing claims (C95-C97). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct testing; peer reviewers accept as part of supported evolutionary interpretations.
Agreement on MSCI escape context claims (C81-C82). OpenEval finds literature integration appropriate; peer reviewers accept as part of evolutionary framework.
Agreement on sexual selection context claims (C87-C88). Both find citations to previous work appropriate for evolutionary context.
Agreement on seed region conservation claims (C98-C100). OpenEval validates PhyloP analysis; peer reviewers accept as part of comprehensive evolutionary insights.
Agreement on human clinical relevance claim (C43). OpenEval notes appropriate literature use with caveat about correlation vs causation; peer reviewers accept without challenge.
Agreement on negative control findings (C52). OpenEval finds this important for narrowing mechanisms; peer reviewers implicitly accept as part of mechanistic characterization.

Agreement on functional interpretation claims (C86). OpenEval finds experimental evidence strong with reasonable interpretation; peer reviewers explicitly support sperm competition enhancement conclusion.
Agreement on sperm competitiveness claim (C85). OpenEval integrates with evolutionary theory; peer reviewers affirm reduced competitiveness in mutants.
Agreement on sexual selection theory context (C84). OpenEval finds integration of theory with data reasonable; peer reviewers accept contextual discussion.
Agreement on methodological context claims (C93-C94). Both find citations to established principles appropriate for study context.
Agreement on methodological principle claim (C93). OpenEval and peer reviewers accept as appropriate methodological context.
Agreement on seed sequence complexity claims (C101-C103). OpenEval validates with luciferase data; peer reviewers accept contextual discussion without challenge.
Agreement on systematic knockout strategy claim (C104). OpenEval finds this key methodological insight; peer reviewers implicitly support through praise of 'impressive' and 'tour de force' work.
Agreement on mating behavior context claims (C105-C108). OpenEval finds logic sound; peer reviewers accept contextual discussion establishing rationale for sperm competition tests.
Agreement on experimental limitation discussion (C109-C110). OpenEval praises scientific rigor; peer reviewers accept without challenge as appropriate acknowledgment.
Agreement on main conclusion about sperm competitiveness (C112). OpenEval finds functional evidence strong; peer reviewers explicitly affirm finding as 'interesting' with important insights.
Agreement on integrative conclusion about shared targets (C111). Both evaluations support this summary interpretation integrating compensation and targeting evidence.
Agreement on MSCI escape functional claim (C83). OpenEval integrates with knockout data; peer reviewers accept as part of phenotype characterization.
